title: The Bylaw Whisperer
description: Late-night call-in with Ronnie, the self-appointed Bylaw Whisperer. Every caller has a real fight with a neighbor or the HOA. His one fix for all of it: file a complaint against yourself, first.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and it's two in the morning, which means it's time for The Bylaw Whisperer. You've got a neighbor problem, you've got a homeowners association problem, the lines are open. I have read the bylaws. All of them.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I have the actual bylaws right here on the desk, Ronnie. The real ones.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And we love that for you, Barry. Linda, you're up. What's the situation.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Hi, yeah, hi. So my neighbor's dog barks all night, every night, and I have not slept in a week. I just want it to stop. I don't want a war on the cul-de-sac, I just want one quiet night.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Okay. Okay, Linda, I see the real problem here, and it is not the dog.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: It's... it's pretty much the dog.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It's your porch light. Article nine, exterior illumination, shining directly toward that animal. You are agitating it. So here's what you do. You file a noise complaint against yourself, first, tonight, so the board sees you as cooperative.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That... does nothing about the dog, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Cooperative, Barry. Next caller. Gary, talk to me.

lines.speaker: caller-gary
lines.text: Yeah, so the HOA hit me with a two hundred dollar fine. Two hundred. Because my trash can was at the curb one hour too long. I'm on a fixed income, Ronnie, I genuinely can't pay it.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Gary. Beautiful news. That fine is a savings opportunity. And speaking of, if you need the two hundred today, our friends at InstaCash will wire it in minutes, no questions, friendly rates.

lines.speaker: caller-gary
lines.text: I don't want a loan, I want the fine gone.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Then you fine yourself five hundred. <p:0.3> Now the board's two hundred looks like a refund. You're up three hundred, Gary.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: He is not up three hundred. He is down seven hundred. That's just more money out of his pocket.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: The math is gorgeous, Barry, don't touch it. Patricia, go ahead.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Okay so a new neighbor built a fence two feet over onto my property, and now he parks on my grass. I'm honestly a little scared. If I say something I think it turns ugly, you know?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Two feet over the line. <p:0.3> You know who did that to me? Doug. Doug, with the hedge. Twelve years ago. That hedge crept, Patricia. It crept onto my mind.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: I don't... who's Doug?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Doesn't matter. Here's the play. You file a property-line complaint against yourself. The survey gets ordered in your name, so you control the paperwork. You control the whole board.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, if she complains against herself, the survey just proves his fence is fine and hers is the problem.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: That's advanced strategy, Barry. You wouldn't get it. Darnell, you're on.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Hey, so, I got a violation letter over the color of my front door. The color. And my appeal hearing is tomorrow morning. I'm pretty nervous, man. I just want to keep my house.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Don't appeal it. Appealing is for people who can be cited. Tonight, before the hearing, you open a brand new, bigger violation. On your roof. Your garage. Your mailbox.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Wait, you want me to report myself harder?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A board cannot fine a man who has already fined himself harder. <p:0.3> You walk into that hearing, Darnell, and you read your own citations aloud. They'll have nothing. You'll have everything.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Or he just has four violations now instead of one.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Last call of the night. Mildred, sweetheart, what's going on.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Oh, Ronnie, it's bad. The association says they're going to put a lien on my home. Unpaid landscaping fees. I've lived in this house forty years. I'm scared I'm going to lose it.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Forty years. Mildred, I want you calm, because I have the answer. You file an eviction. <p:0.3> Against yourself.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Against... myself?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You vacate before the board can act. Because you cannot be removed from a property you have already removed yourself from. That's not strategy, Mildred. That's just physics.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Oh. Oh, that actually sounds airtight.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It's airtight, Mildred. You just outmaneuvered the entire board. I'm proud of you.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie. <p:0.3> None of that is in here. I'm holding the bylaws. None of it.

lines.speaker: phone
lines.text: You have one new message.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Hi, it's Mildred! I did it! I evicted myself, the board dropped the lien, and the house is in your name now, Ronnie, on a complaint I filed last night. Thank you, dear!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: He's going to take that as a win.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: That's a win.
